notes: Page 2 shows only the bag 1 and bag 2 icons (excavator and level crossing) and a safety warning. There are no building steps, so no pieces or joins are added.
Page 3 is a general tips page. It says to build on a table and to open one bag at a time. There are no building steps, so no pieces or joins are added.

Page 4 is the bag 1 intro (excavator) plus a minifigure assembly (helmet, head, torso, legs). The minifigure parts are not in the parts list, so I did not record them. No listed pieces are placed on this page.
Step 1: the base plate looks black but is taken as the Dark Bluish Gray 4x8 plate (lego-3035), the only plate that size in the parts list.

Step 2: four light grey hinge plates (lego-60471) go on the plate ends, two at each end, with the fingers pointing outward. The page shows three placed and one being added. Their exact stud positions are estimated from the picture.
The piece-on-piece contacts are also recorded as joined edges, listed in `edges` because the output format has no rests_on field.
Step 3: two black 1x4 wheels-holder plates (lego-2926) go across the base width, one inside each pair of hinge plates. I took them to rest on the base plate b1 only.
Step 4: two yellow 1x2 plates (lego-3023) go on the base plate between the wheels-holder plates, one against each. Their stud positions are estimated from the picture.
The page gives no clear view of whether the wheels-holder plates also overlap the hinge plates. The hinge plates hold the base's end studs, so I assumed no overlap.

Step 5: two yellow 2x6 plates (lego-3795) lie across the base width, side by side and offset from each other, so each sticks out one stud on a different long side. That offset shows in step 6. They rest on the base plate b1, the wheels-holder plates b6 and b7, and the yellow 1x2 plates b8 and b9.
Step 6: a second dark 4x8 plate (lego-3035) goes on top, resting on the two yellow plates and the wheels-holder plates. The hinge plates at the ends stay uncovered.
Exact stud-level ports are not clear from the picture, so these edges use null ports. Piece placement is approximate.

Step 7: two yellow 30° 1x2 slopes (lego-85984) go on the studs of the yellow plates that stick out past the top plate. The front one rests on b11 and the back one on b10. The picture shows one placed and one being added.
Step 8: two yellow 3x1 curved bricks (lego-50950) go across the two ends of the top plate b12. They sit on its end studs, so I took them to rest on b12 only. This is inferred from the picture.
Step 9 (2x): the callout shows a small black grooved tile. I took it to be lego-2412b, the only black grooved tile in the parts list. One goes beside each yellow curved brick on the top plate b12.

Step 10: hazard-stripe stickers go on the two curved bricks. Stickers are not tracked as pieces. A large black part also appears on the middle of the top plate. It is not clearly shown, so I took it to be the black 4x4 turntable (lego-61485), and the stud positions are approximate.
Each placed piece is recorded with a joined edge to b12 because the output format has no rests_on field.

Axle sub-assembly (steps 1-3) is built twice. Each is a black 1x4 wheels-holder plate (lego-2926), two black clip plates (lego-63868) on top, and a small black train wheel (lego-50254) on each peg end. Wheel colours and types are inferred from the parts list.

Step 11: each axle sub-assembly clips onto the hinge-plate fingers at one end of the chassis. This is recorded as clip-to-hinge joins. Which clip goes on which hinge plate is approximate, following my earlier assignment of b2/b3 to the left end and b4/b5 to the right end.
The clip ports used here are 'clip.1' and the hinge port is 'hinge.1'. The catalogue entry for lego-63868 has clip.1, and lego-60471 has hinge.1 and hinge.2.
Step 12 (4x): each yellow wheel (lego-6014b) gets a black tyre (lego-60700). The four wheels then go on the pegs of the chassis wheels-holder plates b6 and b7, two on each.
Which holder plate takes which wheel is approximate, taken from the picture.
This page starts the excavator cab, built separately from the chassis. Step 1 is a yellow 6x6 plate (lego-3958), b38.

Step 2: the dark plates are uncertain. I took the two lower ones to be 2x8 plates (lego-3034) side by side, overhanging the yellow plate. I took the floating one to be a Dark Bluish Gray 2x6 (lego-3795), the only other dark plate that fits. All three sit in roughly the right place but the exact types and studs are approximate.
Edges use null ports because the stud-level positions are unclear from the picture.
Step 3: the cab is turned over and a light grey round 4x4 plate with a pin hole (lego-60474) is pressed onto the underside of the yellow 6x6 plate b38. It rests on b38.
Step 4: the cab is turned back and a blue 1x4 brick with side studs (lego-30414) goes on the dark plates at the back. I took it to rest on b41 and b39. The studs on its side face outward.

Step 5: three dark 1x2 grille bricks (lego-2877) go around the blue side-stud brick, which appears as a dark wall. One is the floating piece, but the page already shows two beside the blue brick. I assumed all three are placed on this page.

Step 6: a yellow L-shaped layer is built from a 2x6 brick (lego-2456), a 1x4 brick (lego-3010) and a yellow 1x2 hinge brick (lego-30386) at the left end. These types are my best reading of the picture. The yellow 1x4 could instead be the 1x4 hinge brick, and the end piece could be the 2x2 hinge brick with axle hole.
Stud-level ports and exact resting pieces are approximate, so the edges use null ports.
Step 7: two yellow 1x4 plates (lego-3710) go along the front of the cab floor. They look thin, so I took them to be plates rather than bricks.
Step 8: the blue steering stand with black wheel (lego-3829c01) goes on the dark floor plate in the cab, between the yellow plates. I took it to rest on b40.
Stud-level positions are approximate, so the edges use null ports.

Roof/hood sub-assembly (steps 1-4), then attached in step 9 to the cab, which I took to be on the blue side-stud brick b43. Steps: yellow 2x6 plate b53, then a dark 1x4 plate b54 on top, then a trans-red cheese slope b55/b56 at each end, then two yellow 3x1 curved bricks b57/b58 side by side. The red-white hazard sticker in step 4 is not tracked as a piece.

Parts-count conflicts: the yellow 3795 plates and yellow 50950 curved bricks are already used earlier as b10/b11 and b15/b16, so those earlier ids are probably wrong. The two long yellow end pieces carrying the hazard stickers on the chassis (b15/b16) are more likely the yellow 1x4 grooved tiles (lego-2431). b10/b11 may also be other yellow plates. This should be corrected later.
Step 9 attachment details are approximate.

Step 10: a yellow curved wedge brick with 4 studs (lego-52031) is placed on the rear of the cab, resting on b47 and the roof assembly b53. I assumed this because only one yellow 4-stud curved wedge is in the parts list.

Step 11: a dark grate slope (lego-61409) and a black 1x2 grille tile (lego-2412b) go on top of the yellow wedge. The picture shows both, one possibly already in place. The exact studs are approximate.
Step 12: two yellow 1x4 bricks are stacked with a dark 1x4 plate on top, then the stack goes on the cab as a rear pillar. I took it to rest on b47.
Parts-count conflict: the parts list has only two yellow lego-3010 bricks, and b48 (page 14) used one of them. So b48 was probably a different yellow piece, such as the yellow 1x4 hinge brick.
The exact placement on the cab is approximate.

Steps 1-3: windscreen (lego-84954, Trans-Brown), a yellow 4x4 curved wedge brick (lego-45677) as the cab roof, and a trans-orange 1x2 tile (lego-3069b) as the beacon on its two studs. A sticker goes on the roof and is not tracked as a piece.

Step 13: the finished cab top goes on the front of the cab, and the windscreen sits over the front floor plates. The exact resting pieces are approximate, so the edges use null ports where a port is unclear.

Crane arm: a yellow 1x6 hinge brick and a yellow 1x4 hinge brick are hinged together (step 1). A black hinge with towball socket goes on the free end of the 1x4 hinge brick (step 2). The hook with towball clicks into that socket (step 3). The '7936' sticker is not tracked as a piece.
Which hinge finger joins which is approximate.
Step 14: the crane arm hinges onto the yellow 1x2 hinge brick b49 at the front of the cab. No new pieces are added.
Step 15: the finished cab with its arm goes down onto the chassis turntable, which I took to be b19. It locks to the round plate b42 under the cab and can swivel. No new pieces are added.
The arm is shown bent at its hinges. That is a pose, not a new connection.

Step 16: the cab canopy (windscreen b65, roof b66 and beacon b67) is lifted off so the minifigure can be seated, then put back. The minifigure is not in the parts list and is not recorded. The canopy returns to the same joins as on page 19, so nothing new is added.

Step 17: the black towball hinge b70 and hook b71 come off the arm tip. They are shown set aside and are not used again here. The yellow bucket (lego-30394) hinges onto the 1x4 hinge brick b69 in their place.
The earlier joins b69-b70 and b70-b71 no longer hold. They cannot be removed in this output format, so a later pass should treat them as superseded.
Bag 2 (level crossing) starts here. Step 1 places the first straight track piece (lego-53401), b73. It is the first piece of this model, so it rests on nothing.
The callout shows two small plastic sprue pins on the stacked track pieces. They are thrown away and are not parts.

Step 2: two green 1x4 plates (lego-3710) sit on the end sleepers of the track b73, and a light grey 2x4 plate (lego-3020) is added on the middle sleeper. The picture shows the green plates placed and the grey plate being added.
Stud-level positions are approximate, so the edges use null ports.
Step 3: a light grey 1x8 tile (lego-4162) is laid along one side of the track on the two green plates and the grey 2x4 plate, so it rests on b74, b75 and b76.
Stud-level positions are approximate, so the edges use null ports.
Step 4: the track deck is finished with seven more light grey 1x8 tiles (lego-4162). With b77 that makes 8 tiles, 4 rows of 2 end to end, matching the 8 light grey 1x8 tiles in the parts list.
Which green plate or the 2x4 plate each tile touches is approximate. All tiles rest on the track b73.

Step 5: four light grey 10° sloped 6x8 bricks (lego-4515) form the road ramps. Two go on the front side of the track, one on the back left, and one is being added on the back right. They sit on the outer sleeper studs of the track b73.
Stud-level positions are approximate, so the edges use null ports.
Step 6: two more straight track pieces (lego-53401) are pushed onto the ends of the crossing track b73, one at each end. That uses 3 of the 4 track pieces in the parts list.
Tracks connect end to end through their rail ends, not by resting on one another, so these are side joins.

The crossing signal base is built 2x (copies b91-b94 and b95-b98). Each is a green 2x6 plate, a green 1x4 plate laid across one end, and a dark 1x2 Technic brick (lego-3700) with a dark 45° 2x2 slope (lego-3039) on top. The Technic brick's pin hole is for the signal post later.
Parts types for the dark pieces are inferred from the parts list. The tall black block is taken as lego-3700.

Steps 4-6 (2x), on the two signal bases from page 31. Each copy gets a black Technic pin (lego-2780) through the upright tab with a hole, a dark Technic brick 1x2 (lego-3700) on top of the tab, and a black bracket (lego-2436) on its two studs. This is probably the signal head.

This page shows the upright tab piece in step 4 more clearly, and it looks like the dark Technic connector plate (lego-32530) rather than a 3700. The 3700s listed on page 31 (b93, b97) are therefore probably 32530 pieces, because the parts list has only two 3700 and they are needed in step 5. Treat b93 and b97 as the tab pieces carrying the pin holes.
The black bracket type (lego-2436) is inferred from its L shape and the parts list.

Step 7: the two finished signal bases go onto the track. The base with green plates b91/b92 sits on the left track piece b89 and the other (b95/b96) on the right track piece b90. Both sit on the sleepers beside the crossing deck.
No new pieces are added. Which base goes on which track piece is approximate.

Signal lamp head, built 2x (copies b105-b108 and b109-b112). Each starts with a black 2x3 plate, a white jumper plate on one end, and a black grille tile on the rest. A trans-red 1x1 round plate then goes on the jumper stud as the light.
The black piece with a bottom tab in step 2 is taken to be lego-2412b, since five black grille tiles are in the parts list. This is uncertain. The X sticker on the head is not tracked.
Steps 4-5 (2x): a hazard X sticker goes on top of each signal head (not tracked as a piece). A black lance (lego-3849) then clips onto the head's tab as the long signal pole.

The tab piece in page 34 step 2 looks like a black clip plate (lego-63868), but all four of those were used on the excavator axles. I kept it as lego-2412b b107/b111, which has no clip port. So the lance joins use a null port on the head. This may need correction.

Step 8: each signal pole (lance with head, from page 35) is pushed down into the black round 2x2 brick with axle hole (lego-3941) in each base. The round bricks were already sitting in the bases on page 31, where the black block in step 3 is really this round brick. I record them here as b115 and b116, resting on the green base plates b91 and b95.
On page 31 the pieces b93 and b97 are therefore the dark upright tab pieces, probably lego-32530, as noted on page 32. Their types are likely wrong, and the dark slope b94/b98 is probably correct.
The pole joins the round brick's axle hole with its bar. Which pole goes into which base is approximate.

Barrier arm, built 2x (copies b117-b119 and b120-b122). Each is a black 1x8 plate, a white 1x8 tile (lego-4162) shifted along it so it overhangs one end, and a black wedge plate (lego-41770) on the exposed end of the black plate. The red stickers on the arm are not tracked.

The picture shows the white strip overhanging the black plate by about three studs. I took it to be a white 1x8 tile (lego-4162), one of four in the parts list. The other two white tiles are used for the second arm and probably the next page's extension.

Steps 3-4 (2x): the arm built on page 37 is turned over, and a white 1x10 plate (lego-4477) is pressed onto its underside. The plate overlaps the white tile and the black plate, then extends the arm to full length. The picture shows this from below, so it is recorded as joined edges, not 'resting on'.
Stud-level positions are approximate, so the edges use null ports.

Steps 5-6 (2x): on the free end of each barrier arm, a white 2-finger hinge plate (lego-60471) is pressed onto the underside of the white 1x10 plate. A white 1-finger hinge plate (lego-44301a) then snaps onto its fingers, giving the hinge that mounts the arm. Red stickers go on top of the arm and are not tracked.
Which hinge finger joins which is approximate.

Step 9: each barrier arm is attached to the black bracket on its signal base. The black wedge-plate end of the arm (b119 or b122) is pushed onto the bracket (b101 or b104). The picture shows the left arm already fitted and the right one being added.
No new pieces are added. Which arm goes on which bracket is approximate.

Page 41 is a play illustration with no building steps. It shows the finished excavator with the hook arm lifting a loose straight track piece. That is the fourth lego-53401 in the parts list (the other three are b73, b89 and b90), so I record it as an unattached part (b129).
The hook-and-socket arm shown here is the alternative to the bucket, using the hook b71 and socket b70 left over from page 24. I made no new joins.

Page 42 has no building steps. It shows the finished excavator on the level crossing, with the axle sub-assemblies b20 and b25 swivelled so their wheels run on the rails. The swivel is a pose of the existing clip-to-hinge joins, not a new connection.

Page 43 has no building steps. It shows the barrier arms raised and the excavator driving over the crossing, with the axle sub-assemblies b20 and b25 folded up so the road wheels carry it. These are poses of existing hinge joins, not new connections.
Page 44 is an advertisement for other LEGO City train sets (7895, 7896, 7936, 7937, 7938, 7939). It has no building steps, so nothing is added.
Page 45 is an advertisement for LEGO City fire sets (7241, 7942, 7239, 7207, 7208). It has no building steps, so nothing is added.
Page 46 is a parts inventory with no building steps, so nothing is added.

Reading the inventory against my earlier choices: the black 1x4 wheels-holder plate (292626) has 4x, matching b6, b7, b20 and b25. The black 2x2 round brick with axle hole (614326) has 2x, matching b115 and b116. The yellow 1x4 bricks (301024) are 2x, and the yellow 2x6 plates (379524) are 2x. These counts conflict with some earlier assumptions, such as b10, b11 and b53 all being yellow 3795, and b48 and b62 plus b63 all being yellow 3010. The black 1x2 tile with a tab (4282746 appears in the list as 2x) is a black wedge-shaped piece rather than a 2412b, so b17, b18, b61 and the tiles b107 and b111 may need review.
Not needed for the graph: the head (4261301) and helmet (383321) are minifigure parts.
Page 47 is the second parts inventory page, with customer service contacts. It has no building steps, so nothing is added.

It confirms the quantities already in the parts list. Examples are the 4x track (4279714), the 8x light grey 1x8 tiles (4211481), the 4x 10° sloped 6x8 bricks (4211819) and the 2x 1x2 Technic bricks (4211111). It also lists the 2x 1x2 Technic pin connector plate (4210763), a part I may have mis-typed as 3700 on pages 31-32.
Page 48 is the back cover, a survey ad (nielsen.com/LEGO). It has no building steps, so nothing is added.
This is additions only. Earlier entries were not altered, so some mis-typed pieces remain and should be read as corrected here.

Mis-typed earlier pieces: b15 and b16 (chassis end pieces, typed lego-50950) are really the yellow 1x4 tiles lego-2431. The added tiles b134 and b135 are the real ones, and b15/b16 should be dropped. b93 and b97 (typed lego-3700) are really the dark Technic pin connector plates lego-32530, so b143 and b144 are the real ones and carry the pins. b48 (yellow lego-3010) is really the yellow 2x2 hinge brick lego-30389c, so b136 is the real one. The third yellow lego-3795 (b53) is also over the list count, and I could not pin down which yellow plate it really is.

Parts that were missing from the graph and are now added: lego-2376 ring tile (on the turntable b19), two 3068b 2x2 tiles (beside the turntable on b12), a third yellow 1x2 plate b133, a second grate slope b141, the sticker sheet b142 (tied to the roof b66), two 95120 hinge tiles (b137 and b138, the black tabbed pieces on the signal heads that the lances clip to) and two more white 1x8 tiles (b139 and b140, the second white segment of each barrier arm). Their exact positions are approximate.

Connectivity: the booklet's three groups are the excavator, the crossing and the loose spare track b129. They are now linked by contact edges, with an excavator tyre resting on the crossing deck b81 and the hook b71 holding the spare track b129 (page 41-43 illustrations). Nothing is physically fastened across those links, which is why they are contact edges.

Step 5: three dark 1x2 grille bricks (lego-2877) go around the blue side-stud brick, which appears as a dark wall. One is the floating piece, but the page already shows two beside the blue brick. I assumed all three are placed on this page.

Step 6: a yellow L-shaped layer is built from a 2x6 brick (lego-2456), a 1x4 brick (lego-3010) and a yellow 1x2 hinge brick (lego-30386) at the left end. These types are my best reading of the picture. The yellow 1x4 could instead be the 1x4 hinge brick, and the end piece could be the 2x2 hinge brick with axle hole.
Stud-level ports and exact resting pieces are approximate, so the edges use null ports.
Step 7: two yellow 1x4 plates (lego-3710) go along the front of the cab floor. They look thin, so I took them to be plates rather than bricks.
Step 8: the blue steering stand with black wheel (lego-3829c01) goes on the dark floor plate in the cab, between the yellow plates. I took it to rest on b40.
Stud-level positions are approximate, so the edges use null ports.

Roof/hood sub-assembly (steps 1-4), then attached in step 9 to the cab, which I took to be on the blue side-stud brick b43. Steps: yellow 2x6 plate b53, then a dark 1x4 plate b54 on top, then a trans-red cheese slope b55/b56 at each end, then two yellow 3x1 curved bricks b57/b58 side by side. The red-white hazard sticker in step 4 is not tracked as a piece.

Parts-count conflicts: the yellow 3795 plates and yellow 50950 curved bricks are already used earlier as b10/b11 and b15/b16, so those earlier ids are probably wrong. The two long yellow end pieces carrying the hazard stickers on the chassis (b15/b16) are more likely the yellow 1x4 grooved tiles (lego-2431). b10/b11 may also be other yellow plates. This should be corrected later.
Step 9 attachment details are approximate.

Step 10: a yellow curved wedge brick with 4 studs (lego-52031) is placed on the rear of the cab, resting on b47 and the roof assembly b53. I assumed this because only one yellow 4-stud curved wedge is in the parts list.

Step 11: a dark grate slope (lego-61409) and a black 1x2 grille tile (lego-2412b) go on top of the yellow wedge. The picture shows both, one possibly already in place. The exact studs are approximate.
Step 12: two yellow 1x4 bricks are stacked with a dark 1x4 plate on top, then the stack goes on the cab as a rear pillar. I took it to rest on b47.
Parts-count conflict: the parts list has only two yellow lego-3010 bricks, and b48 (page 14) used one of them. So b48 was probably a different yellow piece, such as the yellow 1x4 hinge brick.
The exact placement on the cab is approximate.

Steps 1-3: windscreen (lego-84954, Trans-Brown), a yellow 4x4 curved wedge brick (lego-45677) as the cab roof, and a trans-orange 1x2 tile (lego-3069b) as the beacon on its two studs. A sticker goes on the roof and is not tracked as a piece.

Step 13: the finished cab top goes on the front of the cab, and the windscreen sits over the front floor plates. The exact resting pieces are approximate, so the edges use null ports where a port is unclear.

Crane arm: a yellow 1x6 hinge brick and a yellow 1x4 hinge brick are hinged together (step 1). A black hinge with towball socket goes on the free end of the 1x4 hinge brick (step 2). The hook with towball clicks into that socket (step 3). The '7936' sticker is not tracked as a piece.
Which hinge finger joins which is approximate.
Step 14: the crane arm hinges onto the yellow 1x2 hinge brick b49 at the front of the cab. No new pieces are added.
Step 15: the finished cab with its arm goes down onto the chassis turntable, which I took to be b19. It locks to the round plate b42 under the cab and can swivel. No new pieces are added.
The arm is shown bent at its hinges. That is a pose, not a new connection.

Step 16: the cab canopy (windscreen b65, roof b66 and beacon b67) is lifted off so the minifigure can be seated, then put back. The minifigure is not in the parts list and is not recorded. The canopy returns to the same joins as on page 19, so nothing new is added.

Step 17: the black towball hinge b70 and hook b71 come off the arm tip. They are shown set aside and are not used again here. The yellow bucket (lego-30394) hinges onto the 1x4 hinge brick b69 in their place.
The earlier joins b69-b70 and b70-b71 no longer hold. They cannot be removed in this output format, so a later pass should treat them as superseded.
Bag 2 (level crossing) starts here. Step 1 places the first straight track piece (lego-53401), b73. It is the first piece of this model, so it rests on nothing.
The callout shows two small plastic sprue pins on the stacked track pieces. They are thrown away and are not parts.

Step 2: two green 1x4 plates (lego-3710) sit on the end sleepers of the track b73, and a light grey 2x4 plate (lego-3020) is added on the middle sleeper. The picture shows the green plates placed and the grey plate being added.
Stud-level positions are approximate, so the edges use null ports.
Step 3: a light grey 1x8 tile (lego-4162) is laid along one side of the track on the two green plates and the grey 2x4 plate, so it rests on b74, b75 and b76.
Stud-level positions are approximate, so the edges use null ports.
Step 4: the track deck is finished with seven more light grey 1x8 tiles (lego-4162). With b77 that makes 8 tiles, 4 rows of 2 end to end, matching the 8 light grey 1x8 tiles in the parts list.
Which green plate or the 2x4 plate each tile touches is approximate. All tiles rest on the track b73.

Step 5: four light grey 10° sloped 6x8 bricks (lego-4515) form the road ramps. Two go on the front side of the track, one on the back left, and one is being added on the back right. They sit on the outer sleeper studs of the track b73.
Stud-level positions are approximate, so the edges use null ports.
Step 6: two more straight track pieces (lego-53401) are pushed onto the ends of the crossing track b73, one at each end. That uses 3 of the 4 track pieces in the parts list.
Tracks connect end to end through their rail ends, not by resting on one another, so these are side joins.

The crossing signal base is built 2x (copies b91-b94 and b95-b98). Each is a green 2x6 plate, a green 1x4 plate laid across one end, and a dark 1x2 Technic brick (lego-3700) with a dark 45° 2x2 slope (lego-3039) on top. The Technic brick's pin hole is for the signal post later.
Parts types for the dark pieces are inferred from the parts list. The tall black block is taken as lego-3700.

Steps 4-6 (2x), on the two signal bases from page 31. Each copy gets a black Technic pin (lego-2780) through the upright tab with a hole, a dark Technic brick 1x2 (lego-3700) on top of the tab, and a black bracket (lego-2436) on its two studs. This is probably the signal head.

This page shows the upright tab piece in step 4 more clearly, and it looks like the dark Technic connector plate (lego-32530) rather than a 3700. The 3700s listed on page 31 (b93, b97) are therefore probably 32530 pieces, because the parts list has only two 3700 and they are needed in step 5. Treat b93 and b97 as the tab pieces carrying the pin holes.
The black bracket type (lego-2436) is inferred from its L shape and the parts list.

Step 7: the two finished signal bases go onto the track. The base with green plates b91/b92 sits on the left track piece b89 and the other (b95/b96) on the right track piece b90. Both sit on the sleepers beside the crossing deck.
No new pieces are added. Which base goes on which track piece is approximate.

Signal lamp head, built 2x (copies b105-b108 and b109-b112). Each starts with a black 2x3 plate, a white jumper plate on one end, and a black grille tile on the rest. A trans-red 1x1 round plate then goes on the jumper stud as the light.
The black piece with a bottom tab in step 2 is taken to be lego-2412b, since five black grille tiles are in the parts list. This is uncertain. The X sticker on the head is not tracked.
Steps 4-5 (2x): a hazard X sticker goes on top of each signal head (not tracked as a piece). A black lance (lego-3849) then clips onto the head's tab as the long signal pole.

The tab piece in page 34 step 2 looks like a black clip plate (lego-63868), but all four of those were used on the excavator axles. I kept it as lego-2412b b107/b111, which has no clip port. So the lance joins use a null port on the head. This may need correction.

Step 8: each signal pole (lance with head, from page 35) is pushed down into the black round 2x2 brick with axle hole (lego-3941) in each base. The round bricks were already sitting in the bases on page 31, where the black block in step 3 is really this round brick. I record them here as b115 and b116, resting on the green base plates b91 and b95.
On page 31 the pieces b93 and b97 are therefore the dark upright tab pieces, probably lego-32530, as noted on page 32. Their types are likely wrong, and the dark slope b94/b98 is probably correct.
The pole joins the round brick's axle hole with its bar. Which pole goes into which base is approximate.

Barrier arm, built 2x (copies b117-b119 and b120-b122). Each is a black 1x8 plate, a white 1x8 tile (lego-4162) shifted along it so it overhangs one end, and a black wedge plate (lego-41770) on the exposed end of the black plate. The red stickers on the arm are not tracked.

The picture shows the white strip overhanging the black plate by about three studs. I took it to be a white 1x8 tile (lego-4162), one of four in the parts list. The other two white tiles are used for the second arm and probably the next page's extension.

Steps 3-4 (2x): the arm built on page 37 is turned over, and a white 1x10 plate (lego-4477) is pressed onto its underside. The plate overlaps the white tile and the black plate, then extends the arm to full length. The picture shows this from below, so it is recorded as joined edges, not 'resting on'.
Stud-level positions are approximate, so the edges use null ports.

Steps 5-6 (2x): on the free end of each barrier arm, a white 2-finger hinge plate (lego-60471) is pressed onto the underside of the white 1x10 plate. A white 1-finger hinge plate (lego-44301a) then snaps onto its fingers, giving the hinge that mounts the arm. Red stickers go on top of the arm and are not tracked.
Which hinge finger joins which is approximate.

Step 9: each barrier arm is attached to the black bracket on its signal base. The black wedge-plate end of the arm (b119 or b122) is pushed onto the bracket (b101 or b104). The picture shows the left arm already fitted and the right one being added.
No new pieces are added. Which arm goes on which bracket is approximate.

Page 41 is a play illustration with no building steps. It shows the finished excavator with the hook arm lifting a loose straight track piece. That is the fourth lego-53401 in the parts list (the other three are b73, b89 and b90), so I record it as an unattached part (b129).
The hook-and-socket arm shown here is the alternative to the bucket, using the hook b71 and socket b70 left over from page 24. I made no new joins.

Page 42 has no building steps. It shows the finished excavator on the level crossing, with the axle sub-assemblies b20 and b25 swivelled so their wheels run on the rails. The swivel is a pose of the existing clip-to-hinge joins, not a new connection.

Page 43 has no building steps. It shows the barrier arms raised and the excavator driving over the crossing, with the axle sub-assemblies b20 and b25 folded up so the road wheels carry it. These are poses of existing hinge joins, not new connections.
Page 44 is an advertisement for other LEGO City train sets (7895, 7896, 7936, 7937, 7938, 7939). It has no building steps, so nothing is added.
Page 45 is an advertisement for LEGO City fire sets (7241, 7942, 7239, 7207, 7208). It has no building steps, so nothing is added.
Page 46 is a parts inventory with no building steps, so nothing is added.

Reading the inventory against my earlier choices: the black 1x4 wheels-holder plate (292626) has 4x, matching b6, b7, b20 and b25. The black 2x2 round brick with axle hole (614326) has 2x, matching b115 and b116. The yellow 1x4 bricks (301024) are 2x, and the yellow 2x6 plates (379524) are 2x. These counts conflict with some earlier assumptions, such as b10, b11 and b53 all being yellow 3795, and b48 and b62 plus b63 all being yellow 3010. The black 1x2 tile with a tab (4282746 appears in the list as 2x) is a black wedge-shaped piece rather than a 2412b, so b17, b18, b61 and the tiles b107 and b111 may need review.
Not needed for the graph: the head (4261301) and helmet (383321) are minifigure parts.
Page 47 is the second parts inventory page, with customer service contacts. It has no building steps, so nothing is added.

It confirms the quantities already in the parts list. Examples are the 4x track (4279714), the 8x light grey 1x8 tiles (4211481), the 4x 10° sloped 6x8 bricks (4211819) and the 2x 1x2 Technic bricks (4211111). It also lists the 2x 1x2 Technic pin connector plate (4210763), a part I may have mis-typed as 3700 on pages 31-32.
Page 48 is the back cover, a survey ad (nielsen.com/LEGO). It has no building steps, so nothing is added.
